messages:
srinivas: quick sync — i prototyped an alternate eviction signal that leaks headroom info to the enqueue path. curious about tradeoffs before i file an RFC.

maya: quick summary? what does the signal carry today vs your patch?

srinivas: today we have a boolean 'is_overcommitted' and per-lane token counts. the new signal adds two small ints: soft_headroom_ms and inflight_estimate. soft_headroom_ms is a moving estimate of how long a batch can wait before causing tail latency spikes. inflight_estimate is local in-flight token count including KV cache slots.

jamie: sounds like more state in the hot path. that can be expensive if we read it under the lock on every enqueue. did you benchmark?

srinivas: microbenched on my tiny rig. enqueue qps dropped ~6% with atomic reads, but we eliminate a bunch of late evictions and requeues which saved throughput overall for mixed short/long workloads.

priya: operationally — how do we avoid noisy signals from a single misbehaving tenant toggling soft_headroom wildly? can that starve others?

srinivas: good call. plan is to attach signal to queue-shard not tenant. we compute a decayed EWMA and clamp deltas to +/-20% per second. also combine with admission credits so a tenant can't instantly drain headroom.

maya: how does this interact with cooperative preemption? if we tell enqueue to delay for headroom, will preemptors still get timely slices?

jamie: we should separate goals: enqueue shaping (avoid making batches that will overflow GPU memory) vs preemption (reclaim compute mid-batch). my vote: keep preemption orthogonal and let enqueue signals bias batch formation only.

srinivas: agree. enqueue decides whether to start a new batch or wait; preemption can still abort/steal at runtime. intent is to reduce aborts in the first place.

priya: any new observability? we need metrics to tell when headroom gating caused latency vs saved cost.

srinivas: added gauges: queue_shard.soft_headroom_ms, enqueue.shape_decision_{wait,emit}, and counters for eviction_avoided and eviction_triggered. also a histogram of wait_before_batch_start.

maya: can you paste the config snippet? i want to check defaults.

srinivas: sure:

```
batching: 
  soft_headroom_enabled: true
  soft_headroom_ewma_alpha: 0.2
  soft_headroom_max_delta_pct_per_sec: 20
  inflight_estimate_window_ms: 200
  enqueue_wait_threshold_ms: 6  # default, tuned for p50 latency
```

jamie: the 6ms default seems aggressive for high concurrency. maybe make it model-profile aware? shorter models can tolerate higher wait for better packing.

srinivas: plan: runtime exposes profile tags (short/medium/long) and console can recommend a policy per-model. default is conservative.

priya: edge case: what if soft_headroom is negative (i.e., no headroom)? do we fast-path reject or enqueue and trust preemption?

srinivas: negative => strong bias to emit smaller batches or route to lower-priority lane. only reject if enqueue would exceed hard_capacity. rejected requests fall back to priority queue + fast path.

maya: i worry about complexity of routing fallback. can we keep a single queue but mark batch metadata so runtime can decide packing vs early flush? simpler surface than multi-queue.

jamie: agreed — prefer single logical queue; enrich batch descriptor with flags: packed=true/false, headroom_snapshot. runtime scheduling can pack based on those flags. keeps operator mental model simpler.

srinivas: ok i'll switch to that: single queue, enriched batch descriptors, enqueue uses headroom signal to set pack_hint enum {pack_aggressively, pack_conservatively, flush_immediately}.

priya: please add an audit event when pack_hint==flush_immediately so SRE can track regressions. also add a circuit-breaker if we see >10% of batches flushed for 30s.

srinivas: will do. next steps: i'll update the prototype, run cluster sim against synthetic mixed workloads, and draft RFC with data. any objections to me starting the PR?

maya: go for it. include perf vs rejection-rate tradeoff graph.

jamie: also include a short section on how this interacts with KV cache eviction — we should avoid oscillations where cache evict causes headroom drop which causes packing changes which thrashes cache.

srinivas: noted — i'll add hysteresis and a cache-awareness hook.

infra-bot: deploy-note: srinivas pushed branch "evict-signal-proto" to team/eviction (CI queued) :rocket:

priya: thanks. i'll keep an eye on observability once CI artifacts land. :+1:

srinivas: thanks everyone — filing RFC draft after the sim, pinging for review then. :wave:
